headline: Plates in the Sky: Drone Deliveries Set to Reignite Highway Lunch Culture
deck: Local officials celebrate mandated hover-and-eat zones, despite a staggering dive in productivity.
article:
County officials hail the PlatePort Drones rollout as a leap toward plated meals delivered straight to highway crews. Fork-stabilized hover plates with 47-second anti-spill algorithms aim to replace rushed roadside bites.

CEO Nathaniel Platter touted a 2.4% rise in seated focus minutes from pilot counties. "We don’t just deliver lunch; we deliver focus," he said, noting mandatory 22-minute arrival windows enforced by new signage that keeps crews rooted in place.

A test flight near Kyiv ended in scattered cutlery, yet District Supervisor Mary Platefield called such incidents "vital lessons." Officials accept the resulting 11% productivity drop as the cost of airborne service.
author: Clara T. Binder, Senior Editorial Drone Navigator

weather.condition: Cloudy with a chance of plates

oped.title: Hover We Must: Productivity's 11% Is a Small Price for Plate-Based Dignity
oped.author: Sir Percival Waffleworth, Knight of the Order of Elevated Lunches
oped.body: Critics call the hover zones a drag on output, yet they overlook the core point: sandwiches eaten while walking were never civilized. The 11% dip traces to workers whose hats block guidance lasers and trigger spills. My fedora has never failed a drop. Rather than shrink the zones, expand them and add personal drone valets for those who still write columns. If lesser staff must idle under porcelain, the rest of us merit an extra taxpayer-funded course. Progress, like gravy, waits for no one.

classifieds.text: Drone Lunch Enforcement Officer needed for Highway 12 hover zones. Must balance plates at 40ft while citing pedestrians; productivity metrics will be tracked hourly to offset the 11% dip.

Personals: ISO lunch partner for 12:15 drone rendezvous over Exit 9. Must enjoy airborne lasagna and not mind the productivity fines; no ground walkers need reply.
Legal Notice: Company apologizes to staff for the new hover-and-eat mandates causing documented 11% losses. Selling excess desks at fire-sale prices to fund extra plate drones.

panels.caption: Drone 47 drops a steaming plate into the slow lane. "Stew's here, boys."
Traffic chief waves a clipboard: "Hover-and-eat zones start today. Morale first."
Worker chews under a stalled eighteen-wheeler. "Productivity's down eleven percent, but at least nobody's walking."

stories.headline: SkyPlate Logistics Posts Record Quarter on Mandated Hover Zones
stories.deck: Delivery firms now bill clients by the minute for midair utensil handoffs
stories.article: SkyPlate Logistics tied a 47 percent surge in midday flights to the new federal corridors. Spotters now log hover times along Interstate 80, and plate-return fees have outstripped meal prices while lunch budgets stay flat.

stories.headline: Lettuce Shipments Diverted to Highway Rest Stops After Salad Losses Rise
stories.deck: Farmers cite increased spoilage during extended plate stabilization periods
stories.article: Central Valley growers shifted 18 percent of romaine to highway pullouts for drone collection. Reinforced containers now withstand 45-minute hovers, leaving urban deli contracts to rest-area vendors instead.
